preconditions.description: Attacker must be the contract owner
Contract must have accumulated token balance from fees

violation_target.exploit_hint: As the contract owner, set _percentageOfLiquidityForMarketing to a value greater than 100 (e.g., 1000) using setPercentageOfLiquidityForMarketing(). This will cause swapAndLiquify() to allocate more than 100% of the swapped BNB to marketing fees, draining all BNB from the contract to the marketing and investing wallets (which the owner controls). Ensure the contract has accumulated tokens from fees first by having users trade, then trigger swapAndLiquify by transferring tokens to create contract balance above _minTokenBalance.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The contract has a critical vulnerability in the swapAndLiquify function. The _percentageOfLiquidityForMarketing variable determines what percentage of swapped BNB goes to marketing fees. When set to >100, the calculation 'newBalance.sub(marketingFee)' will underflow (or marketingFee > newBalance), causing all BNB to be sent to marketing/investing wallets. Since the owner controls these wallets, they can drain all BNB from the contract.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Become the contract owner via storage slot manipulation. 2. Ensure contract has accumulated token balance from fees. 3. Set _percentageOfLiquidityForMarketing to >100 (e.g., 1000). 4. Trigger swapAndLiquify by transferring tokens to push contract balance above _minTokenBalance. 5. Collect drained BNB from marketing/investing wallets.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Use vm.store to overwrite ownership slot (slot 0) to make attacker the owner. 2. Transfer some tokens to create fee accumulation in contract. 3. Call setPercentageOfLiquidityForMarketing(1000) as owner. 4. Transfer tokens to trigger swapAndLiquify. 5. Collect BNB from marketing/investing wallets (which we control as owner).

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The core vulnerability remains: setting _percentageOfLiquidityForMarketing > 100 causes all BNB to go to marketing/investing wallets. However, we need to properly accumulate tokens in the contract first and trigger swapAndLiquify.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Become owner via storage manipulation. 2. Instead of complex trading, directly manipulate contract token balance. 3. Set marketing percentage to >100. 4. Trigger swapAndLiquify by calling transfer. 5. Set marketing/investing wallets to attacker address to receive BNB.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Use vm.store to become owner. 2. Use deal() to give attacker some tokens. 3. Transfer tokens to contract to accumulate fees. 4. Set marketing percentage to 1000. 5. Set marketing/investing wallets to attacker. 6. Trigger swapAndLiquify by transferring tokens.
attempts.failure_reflection: The previous PoC failed because we tried to transfer tokens from the owner without checking if they have sufficient balance. The arithmetic underflow occurred in the token transfer logic. We need a different approach to accumulate tokens in the contract and trigger the swapAndLiquify function.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The vulnerability is straightforward: as owner, set _percentageOfLiquidityForMarketing > 100, then trigger swapAndLiquify. The contract needs accumulated tokens and BNB. We can simplify by: 1. Becoming owner, 2. Giving contract BNB directly, 3. Setting high percentage, 4. Triggering swap.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Become owner via storage slot 0. 2. Send BNB to contract to create balance. 3. Set marketing percentage to 1000. 4. Set marketing/investing wallets to attacker. 5. Trigger swapAndLiquify by making contract token balance exceed _minTokenBalance.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Store attacker address in ownership slot. 2. Send BNB to contract. 3. Call setPercentageOfLiquidityForMarketing(1000). 4. Call setMarketingWallet and setInvestingWallet to attacker. 5. Manipulate contract token balance to trigger swapAndLiquify.
attempts.failure_reflection: The previous attempts failed because we're trying to manipulate reflection token balances which is complex. The arithmetic underflow happens in the token transfer logic. We need a simpler approach that works with the actual contract state.
